heroTitle: Preset specialists for people too lazy to configure AI twice.
heroBody: Lazy Agent Shelf turns one high-quality agent source into Claude, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, VSCode, Trae, and generic AGENTS.md outputs.
packsTitle: Install a working department, not a single prompt.

usage.title: These agents are installed into your everyday AI coding tools, not used as a chat box on this website.
usage.body: The website helps you browse, filter, and copy install commands. The actual work happens in Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, VSCode Copilot, Trae, and similar tools.

steps.title: Choose
steps.body: Pick one agent, or install a ready-made pack such as solo-founder-pack.

steps.title: Install
steps.body: Copy the generated command and write the files into your current project or tool config directory.

steps.title: Use
steps.body: Return to the target tool and describe the task naturally; the generated agent, rule, or skill guides the work.

usage.noteBody: Lazy Agent Shelf is an agent shelf: the website is for choosing, the CLI is for installing, and your AI tools are where the agents work.

codex.where: Install as Codex skills, then call the specialist by task intent inside Codex.
notes: Best for repo work, code review, debugging, research workflows, and repeatable local tasks.
Use collections when you want a ready-made working team instead of one specialist.

claude.where: Install as Claude Code subagent markdown files under .claude/agents.
notes: Best for subagent-style delegation inside a project.
Generated files are portable markdown, so you can inspect and edit them.

cursor.where: Install as Cursor rule files under .cursor/rules.
notes: Best for project-level behavior presets and repeatable coding rules.
Use focused agents for review, frontend, backend, product, and naming tasks.

opencode.where: Install as OpenCode agent markdown under .opencode/agents.
notes: Best for terminal-native workflows and repository assistants.
Use --target all if you want to prepare every platform at once.
Best for project instructions that travel with the repo.
Keep sensitive or personal workflow rules out of public repos.

trae.where: Install as Trae-compatible prompt markdown under .trae/agents.
notes: Best for product, growth, Chinese-market, and coding assistant workflows.
The generated prompt remains readable and editable.
